From the given area condition and the Law of Cosines,
\[
\frac12 bc\sin A = S = \frac12(b^2+c^2-a^2)=\frac12(2bc\cos A).
\]
Thus
\[
\sin A = 2\cos A \implies \tan A=2.
\]
Since \(B+C=\pi-A\),
\[
\tan(B+C)=-\tan A=-2.
\]
But
\[
\tan(B+C)=\frac{\tan B+\tan C}{1-\tan B\tan C}.
\]
So
\[
\tan B+\tan C = -2(1-\tan B\tan C)
= -2+2\tan B\tan C.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\tan B+\tan C-2\tan B\tan C=-2.
\]
\[
\boxed{-2}
\]
